record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the tenth International conference on fuzzy set theory and applications (FSTA 2010, Liptovsky Jan, Slovakia)
record.original_question: Let E be a sharply dominating homogeneous Archimedean atomic effect algebra, and let S(E) be the set of sharp elements of E. If S(E) admits an order-continuous state, does it follow that E itself admits a state?

artifact.status_search_result: Literature on sharply dominating Archimedean atomic lattice effect algebras (Riečanová, Niederle, and collaborators) establishes existence of order-continuous states in several special subclasses (e.g., when the compatibility center differs from the center), but a definitive resolution of the stated extension question in the homogeneous (not necessarily lattice) sharply dominating Archimedean atomic case was not located. Status appears unresolved in the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Archimedean Atomic Lattice Effect Algebras with Complete Lattice of Sharp Elements
status_evidence.snippet: Studies sharp elements, blocks and states in Archimedean atomic lattice effect algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Related framework but does not resolve the stated extension question in full generality.

status_evidence.title: The inheritance of BDE-property in sharply dominating lattice effect algebras and (o)-continuous states
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of order-continuous states on sharply dominating Archimedean atomic lattice effect algebras under additional hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive results in special cases; general homogeneous case not settled here.

status_evidence.title: Families of Archimedean lattice effect algebras possessing states
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of families known to admit states.
status_evidence.claim: No general resolution of the posed problem reported.
